Why slow mornings matter

For years I treated the first hour of the day as a sprint. Coffee, inbox, calendar, repeat. It took a bout of burnout to teach me that the morning sets the tempo for everything that follows.

Researchers who study attention call this "attention residue" — the leftover focus from whatever you were just doing. A calm start leaves less residue than a frantic one, and the difference compounds over a decade.

So now I guard the first hour like a trustee guards a fund. No screens, a notebook, and one long walk. The newsletter gets written after, and it is better for it.
